bib.title: Generative Modeling by Estimating Gradients of the Data Distribution
bib.venue: NeurIPS 2019 (33rd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems); arXiv v3 Oct 2020

question: Can a generative model be built by estimating the score of the data density with score matching and sampling with Langevin dynamics, despite manifold and low-density-region problems?
hypothesis: Perturbing data with multiple Gaussian noise levels, jointly estimating scores for all levels, and sampling with annealed Langevin dynamics fixes poor score estimation and slow mixing.
contributions: Noise Conditional Score Networks (NCSN) jointly estimating scores at L noise levels
Denoising score matching objective with lambda(sigma)=sigma^2, usable for model comparison
Inception 8.87 on CIFAR-10 and inpainting by a modified sampler

method.summary: A RefineNet-style U-Net with dilated convolutions and CondInstanceNorm++ takes (x, sigma) and is trained with weighted denoising score matching over 10 geometric noise levels. Images are sampled by annealed Langevin dynamics, T steps per level with step size proportional to sigma^2.
method.task: unconditional image generation (MNIST, CelebA, CIFAR-10) and inpainting

datasets.name: CelebA
datasets.preprocessing: center-crop 140x140, resize 32x32, pixels in [0,1], random flip

models.name: NCSN
models.architecture: 4-cascaded RefineNet (U-Net variant), pre-activation residual blocks, ELU, dilated convolutions replacing subsampling except the first, CondInstanceNorm++ replacing batch norm, average pooling

other.filters: 128 in first cascade then doubled per cascade for CelebA and CIFAR-10; halved for MNIST

models.name: NCSN baseline (single sigma=0.01)
models.architecture: same score network conditioned on one noise level

training.objective: weighted sum over sigma_i of denoising score matching, lambda(sigma)=sigma^2, noise N(x, sigma^2 I)
training.regularisation: random horizontal flip on CelebA and CIFAR-10
training.hardware: 1 Titan XP GPU for MNIST; 2 Titan XP GPUs for CelebA and CIFAR-10

other.checkpointing: every 5000 iterations; MNIST uses last checkpoint; CIFAR-10/CelebA pick lowest FID on 1000 generated images

inference.decoding: annealed Langevin dynamics (Alg 1), uniform noise init
inference.samples: 50000 samples for Inception/FID in Table 1; single run, no seeds reported

parameters.toy_gaussian_mixture: L=10, sigma 20 to 1 (Fig 3); L=10, sigma 10 to 0.1 in Sec 4.3 text; eps=0.1, T=100

other.note: Total network evaluations per image inferred 1000 (L*T)

eval.protocol: 50000 samples; numbers for MNIST and CelebA omitted as not comparable; model selection on FID of 1000 images

availability.weights: checkpoints available at the same URL

results.claim: NCSN reaches inception score 8.87 on CIFAR-10, called state of the art for unconditional models at the time.
results.setup: NCSN, CIFAR-10 unconditional, 50000 samples for scores, checkpoint chosen by FID on 1000 images
results.quote: As an unconditional model, we achieve the state-of-the-art inception score of 8.87

results.claim: NCSN FID on CIFAR-10 is 25.32, comparable to SNGAN.
results.setup: NCSN, CIFAR-10 unconditional, 50000 samples for scores, checkpoint chosen by FID on 1000 images

results.claim: SNGAN unconditional baseline gets FID 21.7 and WGAN-GP 36.4 in the same table (so NCSN FID is worse than SNGAN, MoLM and BigGAN).
BigGAN class-conditional gets FID 14.73 and Inception 9.22, better than NCSN.
Sliced score matching loss on raw CIFAR-10 fluctuates irregularly, but converges when data is perturbed by N(0, 0.0001).
results.setup: ResNet autoencoder, sliced score matching, 50000 iterations (Fig 1)
results.quote: Gaussian noise N(0, 0.0001) we impose is very small

results.claim: Baseline with a single noise level sigma=0.01 and vanilla Langevin fails to generate reasonable images.
results.setup: Same score network conditioned on one sigma, eps=2e-5, T=1000; samples shown qualitatively (Fig 7), no FID reported
results.quote: this baseline fails to generate reasonable images

results.claim: Annealed Langevin recovers the 1/5 vs 4/5 mode weights of a two-Gaussian mixture; vanilla Langevin does not.
results.setup: Toy mixture 1/5 N((-5,-5),I)+4/5 N((5,5),I), exact scores, 1280 samples, L=10, sigma 20 to 1 (App B.1)
results.quote: Langevin dynamics estimate the relative weights between the two modes incorrectly, while annealed Langevin dynamics recover the relative weights faithfully

results.claim: Image sampling hyperparameters: T=100 steps per noise level, eps=2e-5, robust for eps in 5e-6 to 5e-5, uniform noise init.
results.setup: MNIST, CelebA 32x32, CIFAR-10; L=10, sigma 1 to 0.01 geometric
results.quote: We found the results are robust w.r.t. the choice of T, and ϵ between 5 × 10−6 and 5 × 10−5 generally works ﬁne

results.claim: Sliced score matching needs about four times more computation than denoising score matching, due to forward-mode autodiff.
results.quote: requires around four times more computations due to the forward mode auto-differentiation

results.claim: Weighting lambda(sigma)=sigma^2 keeps each noise level's loss on a similar scale, since ||s|| is roughly proportional to 1/sigma at optimum.
results.quote: This inspires us to choose λ(σ) = σ2

limits: Only 32x32 images; only evaluated quantitatively on CIFAR-10.
FID 25.32 is worse than SNGAN conditional/unconditional entries in Table 1 (21.7) and BigGAN (14.73); only Inception is state of the art.
Ignores the Metropolis-Hastings correction: 'we assume this error is negligible'.
Sampling needs L*T = 1000 sequential network evaluations (inferred).
No seeds, wall-clock, parameter count or dataset sizes reported; checkpoint selected using FID on 1000 images.
Architecture design for other domains left as future work.

terms.definition: sθ(x, σ) approximating ∇x log qσ(x) for all σ in a geometric sequence
Langevin sampling run at decreasing noise levels, each initialised from the previous level's final samples, with step size αi = ε σi²/σL²

code.snippet: alpha_i = eps * sigma_i^2 / sigma_L^2; x_t = x_{t-1} + alpha_i/2 * s_theta(x_{t-1}, sigma_i) + sqrt(alpha_i) * z_t
